notes: STATUS: PROPOSED — NOT APPROVED. Nothing in this file authorizes automatic backfill. Per AGENTS.md rule 4, a field is only backfillable when it is explicitly listed in safeBackfillFields, and that list is intentionally empty.

Derived from a read-only comparison of reference lambda-20260714-194920-c3177c97_2026-07-15.json (500 records) against candidate lambda-20260715-080212-d3836a0d_2026-07-15.json (500 records). Full evidence: docs/forensic-bellingham-report.md.

SCHEMA NOTE: two fields were added to the originally-specified schema. (1) 'version' — AGENTS.md rule 7 requires the rule/profile version on every finding, recovery action, export, and Trello draft, and there is no other field to source it from; bump it on any change below, since decisions audited against v1 are not valid under v2. (2) 'collectionPath' — the records path must be declared, never inferred (rule 1); it follows the same convention as ComparisonConfig.collectionPath in src/engine/types.ts, where a root key name selects that key and '$' means the root itself is the array. Say the word if you want either kept out of the specified schema.
KEY SHAPE: primaryKey and dedupeKey are composite — all listed fields joined in order. fallbackKeys is an array of composite keys, each an array of field names.

FACT: source shape is {"Export": [...]}; individual bid records are at $.Export[*]. All 45 fields are present in 100% of records in both runs and every value is a JSON string — including list-valued fields (BidDocuments, BidDocumentHashes, AddendumDocuments, AwardDocuments), which are JSON-encoded strings such as "[]" and must be decoded before document-level diffing.

FACT: both files begin with a UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF) and fail JSON.parse unmodified. This repository parses uploaded text directly at src/workers/analysis.worker.ts:15-16 and src/lib/file-order.ts:15-16, so these exports cannot be loaded by the app as-is. Reported only; no code was changed.

FACT: BidURL is 100% unique and non-blank in both runs (500/500 each). All 1000 values match https://cob.procureware.com/Bids/<guid> exactly, with zero trailing slashes, query strings, fragments, case variation, or whitespace. URL normalization (lowercase, strip query/fragment/trailing slash) is currently a no-op and is specified as defensive only.

FACT: ProjectCode is also 100% unique and non-blank in both runs, and agreed with the BidURL pairing in 499 of 499 shared records. It is the fallback rather than the primary because it is human-facing and demonstrably mutable in the source system (see the 48B-2025-Clone-Clone note below).

FACT: AgentID ("1431") and LegacyAgentID ("3042") are constants across all 1000 records and collide 500 ways in each file. Neither can identify a record alone. AgentID is included in the composite keys solely to scope identity once exports from other agents are analyzed together.
FACT: array position is not usable for matching — only 4 of 499 shared records occupy the same index in both files; 495 shifted, maximum shift 488 positions.

FACT: match rate on the primary key was 0.998 (499 shared, 1 reference-only 3B-2018, 1 candidate-only 33B-2026). minimumMatchRate is proposed at 0.95 to leave headroom for normal churn while still failing loudly on a key regression. ASSUMPTION — requires approval.

FACT — THE REGRESSION: eight fields hold the empty string "" in 500 of 500 candidate records: Title, BidStatus, BidType, PublishedDate, DueDate, AwardDate, ContactEmail, ContactPhone. Measured against populated reference values the loss rate is exactly 100% for each. The differing per-file percentages (Title 100%, BidType 99.2%, AwardDate 97.6%, ContactEmail 48.5%, ContactPhone 34.3%) only reflect how often each field was populated in the reference.

FACT: Description (495/500 populated), ConferenceDescription, and the document fields (349 vs 350 populated) survived intact, and the candidate discovered a new record 33B-2026 with 5 documents fetched. The candidate run therefore authenticated, enumerated, and parsed several page regions successfully. HYPOTHESIS (high confidence): one localized header/summary-block extraction routine failed and emitted its initialized "" default. Confirming the trigger requires the scraper source and current page HTML.

safeBackfillFields is empty BY DESIGN — see report section 6a: there are ZERO comparable pairs for all eight failed fields (no record holds a non-blank value on both sides), so their cross-run volatility is unmeasurable from this file pair and any 'safe' claim would be an assumption. Breaking that circularity requires a second known-good run. Recommended order of promotion, each requiring your explicit approval: (1) ContactPhone — only 2 distinct values across the whole reference, static organizational data, 171 eligible records; (2) ContactEmail — 4 distinct values, 3 being case variants of bids@cob.org, 242 eligible; (3) BidType — closed 5-value taxonomy, 495 eligible; (4) Title — 499 eligible but its cross-run stability is UNMEASURABLE from this pair, since the candidate has no Title values at all.

DO NOT PROMOTE without a specific per-source decision: BidStatus, DueDate, AwardDate, PublishedDate. These are named in AGENTS.md rule 6, and two are demonstrably volatile in this very dataset — BidStatus is precisely the field that legitimately changes between runs (Awarded 488 / Cancelled 7 / Open for Bidding 5), and record 38B-2026's description text changed from 'July 29' to 'August 4th' between the two runs, proving due dates move.

BidDocuments and BidDocumentHashes are listed as manual-review, not backfill, and are structurally ineligible regardless: in the 2 affected records (15B-2021, 7B-2026) the candidate value is "[]", a non-blank string. AGENTS.md rule 3 forbids overwriting it automatically.

ContractValue is listed under manualReviewFields for rule-6 completeness only. FACT: it is empty in 100% of records in BOTH runs and has never carried a value in observed data. There is nothing to recover and no observed format to validate against.

FACT: 22 fields are empty in 100% of records in both runs — Addendum, AwardedVendorName, BidTabulations, BidTabulationHashes, ConferenceInfo, ContactName, ContactTitle, ContactFax, ContractValue, Jurisdiction, Modified, and all IssuingAgency*/UsingAgency* fields. They are deliberately NOT placed in excludedFields: they carry no signal today, but if this export path ever starts populating them that is information worth surfacing rather than suppressing.

excludedFields contains only Created and Refreshed. FACT: these are per-run stamps (reference 2026-07-14 21:48:33/34, candidate 2026-07-15 10:01:07/08/09), identical to each other within every record, and they conflicted in all 499 shared records. Excluding them prevents a guaranteed 100% false-positive conflict rate. ASSUMPTION — requires approval.
FACT — DEDUPE: zero exact duplicates on BidURL, on ProjectCode, or on any composite, in either file. 500 unique values from 500 records in both runs.

FACT: 28 groups of reference records share an identical Title (466 distinct titles over 500 records) — for example six records titled 'Aluminum Sulfate (Liquid)': 29B-2022, 36B-2026, 27B-2024, 35B-2018, 33B-2020, 50B-2023. These are recurring annual solicitations with distinct project codes, URLs, and due dates — all 28 groups have 100% distinct GUIDs and 100% distinct DueDates, and 27 of 28 span multiple years. A Title-keyed dedupe would delete 42 of 500 reference records (8.4%). Against the CANDIDATE, where all 500 Titles are "", it would collapse every record into one group and emit a single record — without raising any error. Title-based or fuzzy-title dedupe must not be used (AGENTS.md rule 5). See report sections 8a-8c.

FACT: the one title group that does not span years — 45B-2025 (due 7/22/2025) and 74B-2025 (due 10/7/2025), both titled 'Arne Hanna Aquatic Center Filter Replacement' — defeats any 'same title + same year = duplicate' heuristic. Two distinct GUIDs eleven weeks apart. The data does not establish why they differ; it establishes only that same-title/same-year is insufficient evidence of duplication.

FACT: 48B-2025-Clone-Clone appears in both runs with its own distinct GUID, and no 48B-2025 or 48B-2025-Clone sibling exists in either export. Records whose ProjectCode differs only by a -Clone suffix must be flagged as possible-source-clone review candidates and never merged automatically — inferring a parent/child relationship from the suffix would be inventing a business rule (AGENTS.md rule 1).

FACT — SEPARATE ISSUE: three records (32B-2018, 15B-2021, 7B-2026) also lost Description and retain only 14 of 45 fields non-blank. Two of them are the same records that lost their document arrays. This pattern is record-scoped rather than field-scoped and should be investigated as a distinct per-record fetch failure, not folded into the header-block regression.

OPEN QUESTION — LOWER CONFIDENCE: both runs contain exactly 500 records, and the candidate gained one while dropping one, which is consistent with a page-size or result cap. This is NOT established: the dropped record 3B-2018 sat at reference index 444 and the gained record 33B-2026 at candidate index 50, and array order is unstable between runs, so no recency-based eviction policy can be confirmed from the data. Verify against the scraper's pagination configuration.

SCOPE: this profile describes matching, dedupe, and review policy only. It authorizes no writes, no exports, and no external actions. The primary remedy for this regression is a fixed scraper re-run; recovery is a stopgap that must produce a new, clearly-labelled artifact per AGENTS.md rule 2.
